fact: The v4 factory defines a token supply of 100 billion with 18 decimal places.
applicability: Clanker v4 factory; originating-chain token creation.
supplementary_information: Supply constant: 100,000,000,000 x 10^18 base units.

fact: The factory owner can enable or disable new originating-chain deployments through the deprecated flag. Deployment also requires the configured originating chain to match the execution chain.
applicability: Clanker v4 factory; deployToken entrypoint.
supplementary_information: The constructor initializes the deprecated flag to true.

fact: A deployment can allocate supply to at most ten enabled extensions. Their combined allocation is capped at 90% of supply, with the remainder assigned to the pool.
applicability: Clanker v4 factory; originating-chain deployment with extensions.
supplementary_information: Allocation denominator: 10,000 basis points. The supplied ETH must equal the sum requested by the extensions.

fact: Pool creation requires an enabled hook, and liquidity placement requires the selected locker to be enabled for that hook.
applicability: Clanker v4 factory; pool and liquidity initialization.
supplementary_information: The factory owner or an admin manages hook and locker eligibility.

fact: The v3.1 SDK accepts a vault percentage up to 30% and a duration expressed in days. Its default vault configuration allocates zero tokens.
applicability: Clanker v3.1 SDK configuration in package 4.2.20.
supplementary_information: SDK configuration rule. Related version: BASE-L4-F006.

fact: The v4 SDK offers an optional vault allocation of 0% to 90% of supply, a lockup of at least seven days and a subsequent vesting duration.
applicability: Clanker v4 SDK configuration in package 4.2.20; vault option.
supplementary_information: Duration unit: seconds. Vesting duration defaults to zero; source documentation describes linear vesting when configured. Related version: BASE-L4-F005.

fact: The v4 SDK offers a Merkle-root airdrop configuration with a lockup of at least one day and an optional vesting duration. The configured amount ranges from 0.25% to 90% of the default supply.
applicability: Clanker v4 SDK configuration in package 4.2.20; airdrop option.
supplementary_information: Amount input: whole tokens. Duration unit: seconds. Vesting duration defaults to zero.

fact: The v4 SDK provides an optional token purchase in the creation transaction, funded with a positive ETH amount. For a non-ETH pair, the configuration supplies an ETH-to-pair swap route and a minimum output.
applicability: Clanker v4 SDK configuration in package 4.2.20; devBuy option.
supplementary_information: The ETH-to-pair minimum output defaults to zero; the documented recipient default is tokenAdmin.

fact: The v4 SDK exposes a presale supply allocation and directs presale deployments through the presale contract.
applicability: Clanker v4 SDK configuration in package 4.2.20; presale option.
supplementary_information: Allocation input: 0 to 10,000 basis points. The converter requires a presale contract in the selected chain configuration.

fact: The fee-conversion locker accepts one to seven initial liquidity positions whose allocations sum to 100% of the pool allocation. Tick bounds must respect the pool tick spacing and supported tick range.
applicability: ClankerLpLockerFeeConversion source version 1; factory-created liquidity.
supplementary_information: Position percentages divide the supply assigned to the pool, after extension allocations.

fact: The hook initializes a Uniswap v4 pool using the configured pair, tick spacing and starting tick. The pool uses hook-controlled LP fees and rejects a native-ETH currency address.
applicability: ClankerHookV2 source; factory and open pool initialization.
supplementary_information: The starting tick determines the initial square-root price. WETH is represented by its ERC-20 address.

fact: The v3.1 SDK defaults to the Base WETH pair and an initial market-cap input of 10 ETH.
applicability: Clanker v3.1 SDK configuration in package 4.2.20; default Base pool.
supplementary_information: This is the SDK initialization input. Related version: BASE-L4-F013.

fact: The v4 SDK defaults to a WETH pair, a starting tick of -230400 when Clanker is token0, and tick spacing of 200.
applicability: Clanker v4 SDK configuration in package 4.2.20; default pool settings.
supplementary_information: At least one configured position must touch the starting tick. Related version: BASE-L4-F012.

fact: The hook provides a public pool-initialization path for tokens outside the factory. This path has no factory locker auto-claim or MEV-module setup and rejects pool extensions.
applicability: ClankerHookV2 source; initializePoolOpen entrypoint.
supplementary_information: WETH cannot occupy the Clanker-token role in this entrypoint.

fact: An enabled pool MEV module expires two minutes after pool creation. While it operates, the hook rejects additions of liquidity.
applicability: ClankerHookV2 source; factory pool with an enabled MEV module.
supplementary_information: Two minutes is the module lifetime limit measured from pool creation.

fact: The standard v4 factory path creates the token, initializes its AMM pool and places liquidity in one deployment call. It has no intervening bonding-curve graduation step.
applicability: Clanker v4 factory; standard originating-chain deployment path.
supplementary_information: This row describes the launch path. Optional presales are recorded separately in BASE-L4-F009.

fact: The static-fee hook uses the paired-token fee when buying Clanker and the Clanker-token fee when selling it. Each configured LP fee is capped at 10%.
applicability: ClankerHookStaticFeeV2 source with ClankerHookV2 constants.
supplementary_information: Contract fee denominator: 1,000,000.

fact: The v4 SDK accepts either static token-side fees or a dynamic configuration with a base fee, maximum fee and volatility-control parameters. Its default is a static fee of 100 basis points on each token side.
applicability: Clanker v4 SDK configuration in package 4.2.20.
supplementary_information: SDK input ranges: static fees 0-2,000 bps; dynamic base fee 25-2,000 bps; dynamic maximum 0-3,000 bps. These schema limits differ from the retained V2 hook caps in BASE-L4-F017 and BASE-L4-F019.

fact: The dynamic-fee hook adds a squared-volatility component to the base fee and caps the result at the configured maximum. It requires a base fee of at least 0.25%, a maximum no higher than 10%, and a base fee no higher than that maximum.
applicability: ClankerHookDynamicFeeV2 source with ClankerHookV2 constants.
supplementary_information: Variable fee = feeControlNumerator x volatilityAccumulator^2 / 10,000,000,000. Fee units use a 1,000,000 denominator.

fact: The dynamic-fee hook combines the estimated post-swap tick distance with retained volatility. Its time filters decay retained volatility or clear it after the configured reset conditions.
applicability: ClankerHookDynamicFeeV2 source; dynamic fee calculation.
supplementary_information: Controls include the reference-tick filter period, reset period, reset-tick filter and decay basis points. The post-swap tick is estimated by simulation.

fact: The hook computes its protocol-fee parameter as 20% of the selected LP-fee value.
applicability: ClankerHookV2 source; protocol-fee calculation.
supplementary_information: Integer formula: lpFee x 200,000 / 1,000,000. The 20% applies to the LP-fee parameter.

fact: Only the assigned operational MEV module can raise the LP fee for a swap. The requested fee must exceed the current LP fee and must not exceed 80%.
applicability: ClankerHookV2 source; mevModuleSetFee entrypoint.
supplementary_information: When the override is applied, the protocol-fee parameter is recalculated from the new LP fee.

fact: The v4 SDK exposes a launch-time sniper-fee schedule with a higher starting fee, a lower ending fee and a decay duration of 1 to 120 seconds.
applicability: Clanker SDK package 4.2.20; option labeled v4.1+.
supplementary_information: Defaults: 666,777 to 41,673 fee units over 15 seconds, equivalent to 66.6777% and 4.1673% using the 1,000,000 denominator. Both endpoints accept 30,000-800,000 units.

fact: The fee-conversion locker requires one to seven reward recipients with positive allocations totaling 100%. Each allocation has its own administrator, recipient and fee-token preference.
applicability: ClankerLpLockerFeeConversion source version 1; reward setup.
supplementary_information: Allocation denominator: 10,000 basis points. Administrator and recipient addresses must be nonzero.

fact: When no reward configuration is supplied, the v4 SDK assigns the full recipient allocation to tokenAdmin and chooses the Both fee-token preference.
applicability: Clanker v4 SDK converter in package 4.2.20.
supplementary_information: The recipient allocation is 10,000 basis points of the rewards distributed through this configuration.

fact: The fee-conversion locker separates rewards according to each recipient's token preference. It swaps the portion requiring the opposite pool token and credits the resulting rewards to the fee locker.
applicability: ClankerLpLockerFeeConversion source version 1; reward collection.
supplementary_information: Preferences select the Clanker token, paired token or both. The implementation assigns the final conversion remainder to the last swap recipient.

fact: The administrator of a reward allocation can replace its recipient, change its fee-token preference and transfer its administrator role.
applicability: ClankerLpLockerFeeConversion source version 1; allocation-specific administration.
supplementary_information: Each operation checks the administrator associated with the selected reward index.

fact: The fee-conversion locker postpones reward collection while the pool's MEV module remains enabled and within its allowed lifetime.
applicability: ClankerLpLockerFeeConversion source version 1; reward collection.
supplementary_information: The lifetime check uses the pool creation timestamp and the hook's module-delay limit.

fact: Approved depositors credit fees by recipient and token using the amount actually received. Anyone may trigger a claim, which clears the stored balance and transfers the tokens to the designated fee owner.
applicability: ClankerFeeLocker source; deposit and claim entrypoints.
supplementary_information: A zero-balance claim reverts. Balance-delta accounting accommodates transfer-fee tokens.
